hook: If you say sorry before you've even finished your sentence — this one's for you.
body:
**If you catch yourself saying "sorry" before you've even finished a sentence — that's not politeness. That's a signal.**

It's a signal you've learned to send — probably very early — that your presence, your opinion, your need, requires a kind of pre-emptive justification. Like you have to apologise for taking up space before you're sure anyone minds.

And here's the part that matters: every time you do it, you send that message not just to the other person, but to yourself. You are quietly confirming: I might be an imposition.

You're not. But the habit keeps that belief alive.

The shift is small but significant. Start replacing "sorry" with "thank you." Not sorry I'm late — thank you for waiting. Not sorry for asking — thank you for hearing me. Same warmth. Completely different signal to your nervous system.

Try it once today. One swap. See what it feels like.

More on this — link in bio.
